text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.
- Norway is against the United Nations holding a costly, global meeting on racism in the year 2000. Norway is sceptical of the practical use of such mammoth meetings.
- The increasing traffic has made the sale of small cars a success in Oslo while sales figures for bigger cars are not as good any more.

- The board of Fokus Bank will probably ask shareholders not to accept a hostile bid by Sparebankgruppen savings banks immediately. Fokus Bank wants to buy time in the hope it can still acquire mortgage lender BNbank.
- Den norske Bank (DnB), which is competing with Fokus for BNbank, has raised its cash offer to BNbank shareholders to 209 crowns, including dividend.
- Norske Skog forestry group will invest 2.8 billion crowns in expanding capacity at its newsprint mill in Golbey, France.
- Strict restrictions on farmed salmon could be the price Norway has to pay to avoid anti-dumping duties from the European Union.

- Fokus Bank is looking for suitors who could thwart an effort by Sparebankgruppen savings banks to take it over. Tomorrow Fokus managing director Bjarne Borgersen will visit major shareholders in London. His bank is also trying to get a bid from Sweden's Handelsbanken or Denmark's Den Danske Bank.
- Sparebankgruppen says it now controls 25.13 percent of the stock in takeover target Fokus Bank through options and share acquisitions.
